extracted.intended_audience: researchers, collaborators, partners, conference participants, and the general public interested in KEMRI activities
extracted.subtask_description: Homepage-level overview of the Kenya Medical Research Institute (KEMRI) describing mission, legal status, research programmes, conference/theme, partnership links, and integrity/reporting channels. Useful for assessing fit for collaboration, funding, conference submission, or partnership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Policy Statement
rubrics_metrics.description: We are committed to excellence and highest standards of professionalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expresses an institutional commitment to quality management and professional conduct; implies that work or collaborations with KEMRI should meet high professional standards and quality expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission — alignment with institutional goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Our mission is to improve human health and quality of life through research, capacity building, innovation and service delivery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects, proposals, collaborations and activities should demonstrably contribute to improving human health and quality of life via research, capacity building, innovation or service delivery to be considered aligned with KEMRI's mission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vision — contribution to Centre of Excellence
rubrics_metrics.description: Our vision is to be a leading Centre of Excellence in Research for Human Health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work that strengthens institutional excellence, builds research capacity, or raises KEMRI's scientific profile aligns with the stated vision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal status and operating framework
rubrics_metrics.description: The Kenya Medical Research Institute (KEMRI) is a State Corporation established in Kenya in 1979 ... operated under the Science Technology and Innovation Act, 2013 as the national body responsible for carrying out research in human health in Kenya. Currently, KEMRI operates under Legal Notice No. 35 of March 2021.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partnerships, contracts or grants must respect KEMRI's status as a state corporation and conform to relevant Kenyan law and institutional legal notices/regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Programme — Biotechnology
rubrics_metrics.description: BIOTECHNOLOGY — Projects areas include: Vaccine Development, Diagnostics, Genetic Engineering, Bioin-formatics…
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals in vaccine development, diagnostics, genetic engineering, bioinformatics and related biotech areas map to this programme; thematic fit with listed project areas strengthens suitability for collaboration or internal review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Programme — Public Health & Health Systems
rubrics_metrics.description: PUBLIC HEALTH & HEALTH SYSTEMS — Projects areas include: epidemiology, behavioural and social sciences, nutrition, environmental/ occupational health, oral …
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Population-level, systems, behavioural, nutritional or environmental health projects fit this programme; proposals should state relevance to these sub-areas to signal programme fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Programme — Sexual, Reproductive, Adolescent & Child Health
rubrics_metrics.description: SEXUAL REPRODUCTIVE ADOLESCENT & CHILD HEALTH — Projects areas include: maternal health, child health, adolescent health, STI’s, Gender Based Violence (GBV), infertility, sexual…
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects addressing maternal/child/adolescent health, STIs, GBV, infertility, and related sexual/reproductive health topics align with this programme and should highlight those links.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Programme — Natural Products & Drug Development
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research on natural products, pharmacognosy, lead discovery and drug development fits this programme; proposals should indicate drug-development stage, natural-product sourcing/ethics, and translational plans where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Programme — Infectious & Parasitic Diseases
rubrics_metrics.description: INFECTIOUS & PARASITIC DISEASES — IPDRP focuses on the following sub-disciplines: Virology, Bacteriology, Mycology, Helminthology, Neglected Tropical Diseases and Zoonotic diseases…
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work in virology, bacteriology, mycology, helminthology, NTDs and zoonoses is a clear thematic fit; proposals should specify which sub-discipline and how the research advances detection, prevention, treatment or surveillance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Programme — Non-Communicable Diseases
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects on NCDs (e.g., epidemiology, prevention, management) belong here; proposers should indicate disease focus, population, and expected health-system implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: KASH Conference theme alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: THE KEMRI ANNUAL SCIENTIFIC AND HEALTH CONFERENCE (KASH) — Theme: The Future of Health: Scientific Research, Innovations, Technologies and Manufacturing for a resilient UHC. Registration for the 16th KASH Conference is now open.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions, abstracts or presentations for KASH should align with the conference theme—scientific research, innovations, technologies and manufacturing aimed at resilient universal health coverage (UHC).

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrity and anti-corruption
rubrics_metrics.description: The Kenya Medical Research Institute upholds high standards of Integrity. We do not condone any form of bribery and/or corruption. Report all cases and/or incidences of bribery and corruption here.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: KEMRI expects ethical conduct and zero tolerance for bribery/corruption in research, procurement and partnerships. Allegations may be reported anonymously, by email or by phone; prospective partners and grantees must adhere to anti-corruption standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborators and partners (engagement/partnership expectation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Collaborators and partners — SEE ALL PARTNERS & COLLABORATORS
rubrics_metrics.guidance: KEMRI highlights existing partners and appears open to collaboration; prospective collaborators should demonstrate complementary capacity, shared goals and fit with KEMRI programmes to be considered.
